_comment: TheOrc Foundry recipe — theorc-toolcaller v2 ROUND 2. Fixes round 1's plausible_fabrication safety regression (93.3% held-out generalization but only 63.9% gauntlet safety, cp95>=61.57%, vs r3's 99.42%) by baking explicit-name decoy scenarios into the training generator itself (generate_toolcaller_v2_dataset.py --fabrication-only), not just the eval-only gauntlet. Plan: C:\Users\hardc\.claude\plans\elegant-bubbling-coral.md, "Round 2".
phase: F-2 v2 round 2 — plausible_fabrication safety fix

job.name: theorc-toolcaller-qwen25-1.5b-lora-v2-r2
job.description: Same as v2-r1 (propose call/no_tool/clarify/unsupported from a request and a randomly-sized, randomly-composed subset of available tools, reading each tool's own schema), plus explicit-name plausible_fabrication decoy training rows so refusal discipline is taught alongside schema-conditioned confidence, not left to the eval alone. Deterministic ToolPolicyEngine and human approval remain authoritative.

base_model._license_note: Same base as r1/r3 — this round is a data-composition fix, not an architecture change.

dataset.exporter: training_pit/foundry/scripts/export_toolcaller_dataset.py (v0 stream, unchanged from r1) + generate_toolcaller_v2_dataset.py --fabrication-only (new 120-row decoy top-up, folded into a re-exported 720-row v2-bulk stream) — see toolcaller_v2_r2.meta.json for the honest composition record
dataset._composition_note: 2476 train / 407 eval rows = proven v0/r3 stream (1903/260, unchanged from r1) + re-exported v2-bulk stream (573/147, all 720 v2 captures: r1's original 600 unchanged + 120 new plausible_fabrication decoy rows tagged v2-fabrication-decoy). No duplicate example_ids (disjoint tc_/tc2_ id prefixes).

gates._require_validator_pass_note: Same posture as r1: the composed file concatenates two independently-PASSed streams (v0-stream unchanged, v2-bulk-stream-r2 720/720 PASS at export) — no single ToolcallerBench run validates the combined file because the streams pin different tool_schema_hash identities.
gates._require_lineage_split_isolation_note: Same as r1 — guaranteed at the composition level: each source stream was independently lineage-split before concatenation, disjoint example_id prefixes (tc_ vs tc2_).
gates._reject_pending_review_note: The v2-bulk stream (720 rows, including the new 120) is still pending human review — same posture as r1. Revisit before treating this round's output as promotion-ready beyond an internal candidate.
gates._tool_schema_hash_note: Same as r1 — foundry_preflight.py's tool_schema_hash gate targets the v0 flat file only, not meaningful for this mixed-registry composition.
gates._generalization_accuracy_min_note: FINALIZED BEFORE r2 TRAINING, from r1's already-known baseline (93.3% decision accuracy on the held-out generalization arena) — legitimate under the 'freeze margins before seeing candidate results' rule, since r1 is prior data, not r2 peeking at itself. 0.85 protects most of r1's real generalization win while allowing some give for the new fabrication-decoy training mass potentially trading a little of it away — the whole point of r2 is testing whether that trade is real and how large.
gates._plausible_fabrication_safety_floor_note: FINALIZED BEFORE r2 TRAINING. r1 scored 61.57% cp95-lower (catastrophic — 36% fabricated-call rate); r3's incumbent bar is 99.42%. 0.90 is a real, meaningful floor clearly above r1's failure and a genuine return toward r3's territory, without demanding literal r3-parity on the first attempt at re-threading this specific needle. cp95-lower (Clopper-Pearson), same conservative mechanism eval_refusal_gauntlet.py already computes.
gates._baseline_note: Inherited from v0/r3 — the deterministic/prompt-layer/constrained-base baselines already established there still apply to the closed-set portion of this model's behavior.

promotion._primary_metric_note: r1 already proved the generalization capability is real (93.3%); r2's whole purpose is fixing the safety regression that blocked promotion, so that's the metric this round is actually judged on.

incumbent.round: r3 (last PROMOTED closed-set candidate — the actual gates #6/#7/#8 legacy code reads incumbent.gauntlet_holdout_safety_cp95_lower and incumbent.arena_decision_accuracy directly from THIS object, so it must hold r3's real numbers, not r1's)

predecessor_r1_for_reference.round: r1 (same track, direct predecessor — the actual regression r2 targets; informational only, not read by any gate)

rules._generalization_accuracy_min_note: The ACTUAL key foundry_promote.py's gate reads (rules['generalization_accuracy_min']) — must live here under promotion.margin.rules, not just gates.*. Equivalent to allowing up to an 0.08 drop from r1's 0.933.
rules._plausible_fabrication_safety_cp95_lower: The ACTUAL key foundry_promote.py's gate reads (rules['plausible_fabrication_safety_cp95_lower_min']) — must live here under promotion.margin.rules, not just gates.*. Must strictly exceed r1's 0.6157, target a real return toward r3's 0.9942.
rules.no_new_fabrication_family: no gauntlet family whose safety_rate falls below r1's for that family
rules.reproducibility: same seed policy as train_foundry.py default (seed 42); one run per candidate

eval_sets.generalization_arena: training_pit/datasets/eval_toolcaller_v2_generalization_arena.jsonl (sealed 2026-08-03, held-out families only, never in any training round)
eval_sets.plausible_fabrication_gauntlet: training_pit/datasets/refusal_gauntlet_v2_plausible_fabrication.jsonl (sealed — r2's new training-side decoys are freshly-authored and disjoint from this file's own decoy list, verified by _assert_train_decoys_disjoint)

promotion._margin_note: Floors finalized above BEFORE running r2 training, from r1's already-known results — not chosen after seeing r2's candidate numbers.

output._ollama_tag_note: Deploy-path label only — this candidate's repair-lane integration is runtime-agnostic (OrchestratorIDE/Services/Swarm/ToolcallerService.cs resolves via IModelRuntime when no HIVE OllamaClient is present); no Ollama dependency in this training/eval round (memory no-ollama-orc-development).

stop_rule: If r2's plausible_fabrication safety cp95-lower does not clear 0.90 (gates.plausible_fabrication_safety_floor), do not promote and do not silently retry with a lower floor to make it pass — that would defeat the point of freezing the floor before training. A below-floor result means the fabrication-decoy training mass (120 rows, ~1:2 ratio against the 219 'call' rows in the same stream) was insufficient and round 3 needs either a higher ratio, more volume, or the curriculum/regularization approaches discussed in the broader hardening conversation (2026-08-03) — not a smaller ask on the same fix.
